Thought: Palladium is element 46 in the periodic table. To find its electronic configuration, I need to distribute its 46 electrons according to the aufbau principle. The noble gas Krypton (Kr) has atomic number 36, so it accounts for the first 36 electrons. That means Palladium has 46 - 36 = 10 electrons beyond the Kr configuration. These remaining 10 electrons would go into the 4d and 5s orbitals. 

Typically, we would expect the 5s orbital to be filled before 4d (giving 2 electrons in 5s and 8 in 4d). However, Palladium is one of the exceptions to the typical filling order. Palladium actually has a [Kr] 4d¹⁰ 5s⁰ configuration, where all 10 electrons beyond Kr go into the 4d orbital, leaving the 5s orbital empty.

So the value of x in [Kr] 4d^x for Palladium is 10.
